alphabet.name: ngang (level)
alphabet.sound: flat, no mark — 'ma' = ghost
alphabet.note: The unmarked tone. Not 'no tone' — a deliberate level pitch, and the one the other five are measured against.

alphabet.name: sắc (rising)
alphabet.sound: pitch rises sharply — 'má' = mother
alphabet.note: Rises like the end of an English question, but faster and only on the vowel.

alphabet.name: huyền (falling)
alphabet.sound: low and drifting down — 'mà' = but

alphabet.name: hỏi (dipping)
alphabet.sound: dips then rises — 'mả' = tomb
alphabet.note: The hook is not a question mark. In the north it dips and comes back up; in the south it is closer to a plain low tone.

alphabet.name: ngã (broken)
alphabet.sound: rises with a catch in the middle — 'mã' = horse
alphabet.note: There is a glottal stop inside this one. Northern speakers make it clearly; many southern speakers merge it with hỏi.

alphabet.name: nặng (heavy)
alphabet.sound: short, low, cut off — 'mạ' = rice seedling
alphabet.note: The dot means the syllable is squeezed short and stops abruptly.

alphabet.name: ơ
alphabet.sound: like the 'u' in 'fur', with no r

alphabet.name: ư
alphabet.sound: an 'oo' said with the lips spread, not rounded
alphabet.note: English has no equivalent. Say 'ee' and then, without moving your lips, pull your tongue back.

alphabet.name: â
alphabet.sound: a short 'uh'

alphabet.name: ă
alphabet.sound: a very short 'a'

alphabet.name: ê
alphabet.sound: like the 'ay' in 'day', without the glide

alphabet.name: ô
alphabet.sound: like the 'o' in 'go', without the glide

alphabet.name: đ
alphabet.sound: an English 'd'
alphabet.note: This is the ordinary d. The letter written 'd' is NOT — see below. Getting these two the wrong way round is the most common early mistake.

alphabet.name: d
alphabet.sound: a 'z' in the north, a 'y' in the south
alphabet.note: Never an English d. 'Dạ' (the polite yes) is 'za' in Hanoi and 'ya' in Saigon.

alphabet.name: ng
alphabet.sound: the 'ng' of 'singer' — and it can start a word
alphabet.note: English only puts this sound at the end of a syllable. Vietnamese starts words with it: Nguyễn, ngon, ngủ.

alphabet.name: nh
alphabet.sound: like the 'ñ' in 'señor'

alphabet.name: x
alphabet.sound: an 's'

alphabet.name: gi
alphabet.sound: a 'z' in the north, a 'y' in the south

alphabet.name: tr
alphabet.sound: a 'ch' said with the tongue curled back

alphabet.name: ph
alphabet.sound: an 'f'
alphabet.note: Which is why phở is 'fuh', not 'poh'.
